chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Baziʿ claims that he is a prophet. He said: “If you hear him saying that, then kill him.” He said: So I sat [waiting] more than once, but that was not made possible for me.

key_terms.إِنْ سَمِعْتَهُ: if you hear him; conditional instruction based on direct hearing
key_terms.فَاقْتُلْهُ: then kill him; an imperative legal instruction in this report
key_terms.فَلَمْ يُمْكِنِّي: it was not possible for me; I was unable
key_terms.نَبِيٌّ: a prophet; here, a false claim to prophethood

ai.seo_question: What does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām narrate about the ruling on someone who claims to be a prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a statement to Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man claiming prophethood, and the Imam gives a ruling concerning him. It appears in the chapter on the legal punishment of the apostate, indicating its significance in jurisprudential discussions on ridda and false claims to prophethood.
